analysis.title: Thursday Was Biggest Put Day In Cboe History
key_insights: More than 11.2 million puts traded on the Cboe on Thursday (Nov 5, 2026), the largest put volume day on record, above the prior high of 10.22 million on April 4, 2025.

Index puts hit a record 6.27 million contracts versus the prior high of 5.33 million on Oct 16. Single-stock puts were 2.43 million, the 4th largest day, below the 3.07 million on Oct 10, 2025. The remaining roughly 2.5 million are inferred to be mostly ETF puts.

Eight of the ten biggest Cboe put days have occurred in 2026 and the other two in 2025. Three came in the past three weeks (Nov 5, Oct 30, Oct 16). The 20-day average put volume has roughly tripled since 2020.

Goldman's Coppersmith says clients dumped protection into Wednesday's post-midterm rally, leaving the market underhedged ahead of Thursday's reversal. Forced liquidations across hedge funds then triggered a scramble to buy protection back.
The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4%, its worst day since March 16, 2020. The S&P 500 fell 4.4%, its worst day since Liberation Day. Goldman Prime described a broad drawdown led by tech.

Goldman's Vol Panic Index rose to 9.57 out of 10, a roughly 5-point jump and the 3rd largest daily increase ever, after Wednesday's 4th largest drop. The two-day round trip of 8.55 points is a record, beating 7.87 in April 2013.

VVIX rose about 45 points to 135, its 2nd largest one-day increase after February 2018. VIX closed at about 27. VXN rose more than 13 points (+52.6%) to 38.26, its highest close since April 2025. VXSMH had the largest one-day change in its history, and the VIX curve moved from contango to sharp backwardation.
13 of Goldman's AI-related baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT, led by Optical Networks (-15.3%) and Memory (-15.2%).
US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% on Thursday, the largest one-day increase since March and the third largest in five years, led by large-cap equity ETFs.

Fundamental L/S hedge funds lost 1.3% (-2 SD), US-focused funds lost 1.7%, TMT funds lost more than 4% and multi-strats lost 1.4%. Systematic L/S gained 0.2%. TMT funds have erased their 2026 gain, down from about +24% before the summer.

Goldman Prime says single-stock flows show no sign of panic or faster de-grossing (global de-grossing for a 4th session at -0.5 SD), so discretionary hedge funds were not the main driver of the selloff. Global AI stocks were net sold for a 6th straight session (-2.6 SD), and the 20-day pace of hedge fund AI selling is the largest in over five years (-3.0 SD).
Hedge fund gross leverage is 314.2% (97th percentile over 5 years) and net leverage is 71.8% (4th percentile over 1 year).

Vanda reports retail sold a net $338 million of single stocks, the largest one-day outflow outside March 2020. Seven of the top 10 retail selling days since 2020 are in 2026. Remaining retail buying was concentrated in TQQQ and SOXL. JPM said retail had sold nearly $1.3bn by noon (-6.2z), and its TMT trader called it a -7.2z event.

Levered ETFs faced an estimated $42-48 billion of forced selling into the close. Nomura's McElligott confirmed the final rebalance at -$48.6 billion, the 2nd largest on record. Vol-target funds also de-risked.
Vanda expects CTAs to turn short after the Nasdaq broke 27,600. A clean break below 26,800 would take CTA exposure to Liberation Day lows.
JPM's grid/AI power basket traded more than half a billion shares over two days, against about 320 million at the DeepSeek peak, with a 16% two-day drawdown, the largest since March 2020.
After 15 prior Vol Panic Index signals above 9.5, the S&P averaged +4.6% over 3 months (80% hit rate) and +9.0% over 6 months (73%). One month later it averaged +0.68% (67% hit rate).

JPM's Tyler stays Tactically Bullish. The Nasdaq 100 has tended to rebound about 3% the following week when within ~6% of its high and down 3.5% or more in a day. Armbrust notes the S&P has been higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950 and warns negative gamma leaves scope for violent moves in either direction.

Payrolls rose 165K on Friday, beating estimates and putting a December rate hike back in play. The author argues the base rates assume Fed easing and expects the bounce to be sold as hedges are rebuilt.

sector_views.rationale: AI baskets had record down days, hedge funds are selling AI at the fastest 20-day pace in over five years, and retail has pulled out of single-stock tech. Goldman's desk calls the setup technically poor with large near-term tails.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The print beat estimates and put a December Fed rate hike back in play, which undercuts the case that the Fed will ease to support equities.
The reading is above the 9.5 panic threshold. Prior signals above 9.5 were followed by positive S&P returns over 3 to 6 months, but only a modest one-month gain.

risk_factors: Negative gamma could produce violent moves in either direction.
CTA selling if the Nasdaq breaks below 26,800.
Hedges rebuilt after the panic could be sold into the bounce, setting up another leg down.
A December rate hike is back in play after the payrolls beat, removing the expected Fed easing.
Continued hedge fund selling of AI stocks, with gross leverage at the 97th percentile.
Retail has stopped buying dips in single names.
vol_and_positioning: Record put volume of more than 11.2 million on the Cboe, with index puts at a record 6.27 million.
Goldman Vol Panic Index at 9.57, the 3rd largest daily increase ever. Its 10-day volatility is at an all-time high.
VVIX at 135, up about 45 points. VIX at about 27. VXN at 38.26, up 52.6%. VXSMH had the largest one-day change in its history.
The VIX curve moved from contango to sharp backwardation.
US-listed ETF shorts rose 7%, the largest one-day rise since March.
Hedge fund gross leverage is 314.2% (97th percentile over 5 years), net leverage is 71.8% (4th percentile over 1 year).
Levered ETF rebalance of -$48.6 billion, the 2nd largest on record. Vol-target funds also de-risked.
CTAs are expected to turn short, with a break below 26,800 on the Nasdaq taking exposure to Liberation Day lows.
Negative gamma leaves scope for violent moves in either direction (Armbrust).
geopolitical: US midterm elections and Democratic control of Congress are cited as uncertainty over the value of the AI buildout.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Rich Privorotsky bet on 1998 over 2000 (Fed easing), which the author argues payrolls undermined.
Goldman's Coppersmith is cautiously constructive while JPM's Tyler stays Tactically Bullish.
Vanda's scenario map has the big down tape as the base case after the crash.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Coppersmith and JPM's Tyler argue the drop was a technical and forced re-hedging event, not a fundamental break. Past Vol Panic signals above 9.5 were followed by S&P gains of 4.6% over 3 months. The Nasdaq 100 has tended to rebound about 3% the following week after similar declines.
tension_points.bear_case: The author argues the historical base rates came from episodes when the Fed was easing, and the payrolls beat of 165K puts a December hike back in play. Hedges rebuilt now may be sold into the bounce, and the AI trade has no clear valuation with Democrats controlling Congress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A clean Nasdaq break below 26,800 would take CTA exposure to Liberation Day lows.

theme_stances.key_argument: The author expects the bounce to be used by newly hedged holders to sell into strength before another leg down.
